summary: Robustness Tier 2 (security depth), sprint 2026-W26, iteration 1. Ships MFA/TOTP (all accounts, role-mandatory) and access-token revocation + refresh lifecycle caps; multi-device sessions (2b) deferred to the Redis iteration. Waves continue the Tier-1 numbering (Tier 1 used waves 1-3). Wave 4 = the two foundations that both edit User.java (MFA model V3, revocation epoch/jti V4) — sequenced to avoid a User.java merge conflict. Wave 5 = the MFA flow chain (enrol/activate, login challenge, disable, role enforcement) which shares the MFA service + login flow, run sequentially. Wave 6 = revocation app-layer (admin revoke, refresh absolute cap) which touch different files and run in parallel.

waves.label: Wave 4 — Foundations (MFA model + revocation epoch)
waves.blurb: #28 (MFA model + V3) and #33 (jti + tokens_invalid_before + V4) both add columns to users/User.java — run one at a time to avoid a merge conflict on the entity. Each is the base for its feature's later issues.

waves.label: Wave 5 — MFA flows
waves.blurb: Enrol/activate (#29) -> login challenge LOCAL+social (#30) -> disable (#31) -> role-mandatory enforcement (#32). Share the MFA service and the login flow (AuthService/OAuth2SuccessHandler), so sequential. All depend on #28.

waves.label: Wave 6 — Revocation app-layer (parallel)
waves.blurb: #34 (admin revoke endpoint, AdminController) and #35 (refresh absolute-lifetime cap, RefreshTokenService + V5) touch different files and only depend on Wave 4's #33 — can run concurrently.
